Do not edit any project file except this handoff; do not commit or push. For each item Q7-Q11, R2, R3 confirm or correct your pass-2 answer.

findings.item: Q10 (every wait has a limit) - I2 of step 04e, judged; for the defects of step 10
findings.what: Once the group is gone, stop() waits for the exit event with no limit. Only a fake child of deps.spawn that never sends exit reaches it: trial 14 (pid 999999, a link printed, stopTimeoutMs 300) - stop() still waiting after 3002 ms. With a real child the group is seen gone only after its leader is reaped, and Node emits exit in the same callback that reaps it, so the wait ends at once; a test with a bad fake ends by its own test timeout. Not Medium: no real path hangs.
findings.fix: Race state.exited with a short limit (for example GONE_WAIT_MS) and treat a missing end as unknown, as the F5 guard does.

findings.item: Q10 - I3 of step 04e, judged (AP-014, the kind of L5 in the released kit); for the defects of step 10
findings.place: tools/test/e2e/kit/runner.js:241 (fileTimeoutMs), cleanup.js:282 (hookLimitMs), browser.js:294 (startTimeoutMs), cdp.js:43 and :191 (call timeouts), page.js:195 and :278-292 (timeoutMs, pollMs)
findings.what: These options are not range-checked. By reading the code (not run): a value above 2147483647, 0, NaN or a non-number makes a timer fire after 1 ms, so the wait ends early with the kit's own error (SPEC_TIMEOUT, START_TIMEOUT, CALL_TIMEOUT, NAVIGATION_FAILED) or the signal hooks are cut short before the clean-up; in page.js waitFor a NaN timeoutMs gives a deadline that is never reached, so the wait ends only by the runner's 120 s watchdog. Every case fails closed: no check is skipped and no process is left; the callers are the kit's own specs and tests.
findings.fix: Apply the 1-2147483647 whole-number check of stand.js to each of these options, as one defect for the released kit files.

findings.item: message words - I4 of step 04e, judged; not a security item
findings.place: tools/test/e2e/kit/stand.js:60 ('the options must be an object') and :98 ('env must be an object')
findings.what: An array is refused correctly (USAGE, 0 spawns - trial 4 'options array', trial 1 'env array'), but the words say 'an object', which an array is in JavaScript; the rule broken is 'a plain object, not a list'.
findings.fix: Say 'must be a plain object, not a list' in both messages.
